Θεῷ· Ἀντιλήπτωρ μου εἶ ∆ιὰ τί μου ἐπελάθου; Καὶ ἵνα τί σκυθρωπάζων πορεύομαι,

οἱ ἐχθροί μου ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτούς μοι καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν· Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ Θεός σου;
Οὐχ ὁρῶμεν δὲ πάντες πῶς ἐλεεῖ ὁ Θεός. Καὶ πολ λάκις πρὸς τὰ κατ' ἐλεημοσύνην
αὐτοῦ γινόμενα, τῷ ἐπίπονα εἶναι, οὐχ ἡδέως ἔχοντες, οὐδὲ ἔλεον εἶναι νομίζομεν.
∆ιὸ λέγομεν· ∆ιὰ τί μου ἐπελάθου; Ὁ δὲ διειληφὼς, ὅτι πᾶν ὃ ἐπάγει ὁ Θεὸς
συμφερόντως ἐπάγει, οὐδὲν ἐρεῖ τοιοῦτον, εἰδὼς, ὅτι τὴν μετάνοιαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὴν
ὠφέλειαν πραγματευόμενος ὁ Θεὸς, τοῦτο ποιεῖ. Ἀλλ' ὅπερ ἐλέγομεν, ὁ
μεταγινώσκων λαὸς πυνθάνεται τοῦ. Θεοῦ, διὰ τί αὐτὸν ἐγκαταλέλοι πεν οὕτως
ἐκθλιβόμενον καὶ σκυθρωπάζοντα. Τί τὸ αἴτιον τῆς τοιαύτης ἐγκαταλείψεως; οὐ τὸ
τυχὸν γὰρ ἔοικεν εἶναι. Ὁ μέντοι λέγων· ∆ιὰ τί μου ἐπ ελάθου; θαῤῥεῖν ἔοικεν, ὡς
μηδὲν πεποιηκὼς, δι' ἃ ἐπιλανθάνεται ὁ Θεός. Πάνυ δὲ λυπεῖ τὸν δίκαιον τὸ, Ποῦ; ἐπὶ
Θεοῦ λεγόμενον, ὅπερ ἐστὶ σημαντικὸν τόπου. Τῆς γὰρ ἐσχάτης ἀνοίας τὸ ἐν τόπῳ
νομίζειν εἶναι τὸν Θεόν. Ὄγκῳ γὰρ συνυφίσταται τόπος· ὄγκου δὲ τὸ Θεῖον
ἐλεύθερον. Οὗτοι δὲ τῆς εὐχῆς οἱ λόγοι καὶ τῷ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι λαῷ ἁρμόζουσιν. Ἀεὶ
γὰρ, φησὶ, 17.137 τῆς σῆς προνοίας τυχὼν, καὶ νῦν γυμνωθεὶς, ἀποδύ ρομαι, μὴ
φέρων τοὺς πολεμίους ἐπὶ πληγαῖς καὶ δεσμοῖς καὶ τῶν ἐμῶν ὀστέων τῇ συντριβῇ
λέγοντας· Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ Θεός σου; διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν ταῦτά με πάσχειν
ὑπολαμβάνοντας. Ἠθικώτερον δέ· Ὅταν οἱ ἐχθροὶ ἡμῶν δαίμονες διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας
τὰ ὀστᾶ ἡμῶν συντρίψωσι, τουτέστι τὰς τῆς ψυχῆς δυνάμεις· τότε τὸν Θεὸν ἐπίτηδες
πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὡς ἀσθενῆ διαβάλ λουσιν, ἵνα, τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλπίδος ἀποστήσαντες,
αἰχμαλώτους καὶ δούλους παραλάβωσι. Καὶ τοῦτο καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν, τουτέστι
διηνεκῶς, ποιοῦσι. Τί οὖν χρὴ ποιεῖν; Μὴ ἐκπίπτειν εἰς ἀπόγνωσιν· ἀλλ' ἐλπίζειν ἐπὶ
τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ Θεοῦ, καθὼς ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς διδασκόμεθα. ΨΑΛ. Νʹ. Στίχ. ζʹ. Ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἐν
ἀνομίαις συνελήφθην. Οὐκ ἐν τῇ γαστρὶ μόνον, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ παρέλαβόν με τὰ ἔργα
τῆς ἀνομίας, τὰ τοῦ φόνου, καὶ τὰ τῆς ἀλλοτρίας κοίτης ἣν παρανόμως ἐσύλησα.
Στίχ. ηʹ. Ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἀλήθειαν ἠγάπησας. Ὁ νοῦς οὗτος· Σὺ, φησὶ, Κύριε, ἀληθὴς ὢν καὶ
ἀλήθειαν ἀγαπῶν, βουλόμενος ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διά γειν, ἀποκαθαριεῖς ἡμᾶς τῆς
ἀρχαίας ἁμαρτίας· καὶ οὕτως ἀποκαθαρίσεις ὡς ὑπὲρ χιόνα λευκανθῆναι· ἡ δὲ
ἀποκάθαρσις ἡμῖν δι' ὑσσώπου γενήσεται· ὑσσώπῳ δὲ ἡ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος
ἐνέργεια ἀφο μοιοῦται, θερμαίνουσα καὶ πάντα τὸν ἐν ἡμῖν ῥύπον ἀποσμήχουσα·
pass_a_gloss: He has fallen, rise up. For those who have fallen mourn, and after having sinned they became insensitive, and having delivered themselves over to every sin. In innocence, among men be crowned. Have you fallen among boys? Contend in the noble contest, and conquer in it. In the womb Jacob supplanted Esau; from childhood Daniel prophesied, and he examined the elders. Are you unable to become such? Become next an athlete, as the righteous one, who, even if he falls while wrestling or running, is not shaken, because the Lord steadies his hand. The word is doubtful: whether for his own, or for the one wrestling and already about to be shaken, in order that he may not at all come face forward, and become lying wholly on the ground. Verse 25. I became younger; and indeed I grew old; and I did not see a righteous one abandoned. But otherwise we know age according to the inner man: child, youth, elder. Therefore before Abraham the longer-lived ones of him are not called elders; but he himself first by virtue was made elder, and by having inactivated the inner man of himself the things of the infant. And hear Jeremiah: Do not say, that I am younger. Such a thing concerns me and also David: He says, I became like a child according to the inner man of me. But having changed from youthful character and instability, in which being made younger I was, I came into old age, having a life unfruitful and a gray mind. And thus proceeding, I did not see a righteous one abandoned. If you hear bodily, it is false. There are two kinds of abandonment: the bodily, which does not harm us at all; and the of the soul, which is destructive. As much therefore as we are enriched by righteous works, by so much more We help ourselves so as not to be abandoned until the end. Therefore you are not in, having been abandoned, but having been left behind. Since, at the opportune time, the just are abandoned, as was Job, so that the just may be revealed. Psalm 42. Verse 14. I will cry to God: My helper, why have you forgotten me? And why, being sorrowful, do I go, in the subduing of the enemy? Verse 15. In the breaking of my bones, my enemies reproach me, saying to me every day: Where is your God? But we do not all see how God shows mercy. And often, regarding his merciful deeds, being burdensome, we do not have them gladly, nor do we consider them to be mercy. Therefore we say: Why have you forgotten me? But the one who has received, that everything which God brings upon is beneficial, will not say such a thing, knowing that he is bringing about repentance and benefit, practicing it. But what we said, the people who come to know inquire of God, why he has abandoned him thus, being crushed and sorrowful. What is the cause of such abandonment? It does not seem to be chance. However, the one saying, 'Why have you forgotten me?' seems to be confident, as having done nothing, for which God forgets. But very much it grieves the just one, the 'Where?' being said about God, which is significant of place. For the extreme folly is to think that God is in a place. For place is constituted by bulk, and the divine is free of bulk. But these words of the prayer also harmonize with the people in Babylon. For always, he says, 17.137, having attained your providence, and now being stripped, I undress, not bringing my enemies upon blows and bonds and the breaking of my bones. saying: Where is your God? Because of the weakness these things happen to me, they suppose. But more ethically: When our enemies, the demons, through sin break our bones, that is, the powers of the soul, then they deliberately slander God toward us as weak, so that, having abandoned hope toward him, they may take us as captives and slaves. And they do this every day, that is, continuously. What then must we do? Not fall into despair; but hope in the mercy of God, as we are taught in the following. Psalm 51. Verse 7: Behold, I was brought forth in iniquities. Not in the womb only, but because I received the works of iniquity, those of murder, and those of the illicit bed which I violently plundered. Verse 8: Behold, I have loved truth. This mind: You, Lord, being true and loving truth, wishing to lead us into truth through the earth, you cleanse us from the ancient sin; and thus you will cleanse us as to be whiter than snow; but the cleansing for us will happen through hyssop; and hyssop, the energy of the Holy Spirit is likened to it, warming and cleansing all the filth in us.

In the womb Jacob supplanted Esau; from childhood Daniel prophesied, and he examined the elders. Are you unable to become such? Become next an athlete, as the righteous one, who, even if he falls while wrestling or running, is not shaken, because the Lord steadies his hand. The word is doubtful: whether for his own, or for the one wrestling and already about to be shaken, in order that he may not at all come face forward, and become lying wholly on the ground. Verse 25. I became younger; and indeed I grew old; and I did not see a righteous one abandoned. But otherwise we know age according to the inner man: child, youth, elder. Therefore before Abraham the longer-lived ones of him are not called elders; but he himself first by virtue was made elder, and by having inactivated the inner man of himself the things of the infant. And hear Jeremiah: Do not say, that I am younger. Such a thing concerns me and also David: He says, I became like a child according to the inner man of me. But having changed from youthful character and instability, in which being made younger I was, I came into old age, having a life unfruitful and a gray mind. And thus proceeding, I did not see a righteous one abandoned. If you hear bodily, it is false. There are two kinds of abandonment: the bodily, which does not harm us at all; and the of the soul, which is destructive. As much therefore as we are enriched by righteous works, by so much more

We support ourselves to avoid being deserted until the end. Therefore, you are not one who has been abandoned, but one who has been left behind. For at the proper time, even the righteous are forsaken, as Job was, so that their righteousness may be made evident. In Psalm 42, verse 14, I cry out to God: My defender, why have you forgotten me? And why, while overwhelmed with grief, do I continue forward, in the act of subduing the foe? Verse 15 describes how, when my bones are broken, my adversaries taunt me daily, asking: Where is your God? Yet we do not all perceive how God extends compassion. Moreover, concerning His merciful actions, which often feel burdensome, we do not receive them with joy, nor do we regard them as true mercy. Hence we ask: Why have you forgotten me? But the one who has understood that all God brings upon us works for our good will not speak this way, recognizing that He is fostering repentance and benefit, actively bringing it about. Nevertheless, those who are coming to know God question why He has forsaken the one who is crushed and sorrowful in this manner. What is the reason for such abandonment? It does not appear to be random. On the contrary, the one who cries, 'Why have you forgotten me?' seems to act with assurance, as if having done nothing that would cause God to forget. Yet this question deeply distresses the righteous, especially when phrased as 'Where?' in relation to God, for it carries significant spatial implication. Indeed, the utmost folly lies in believing that God is confined to a location, since location arises from material extension, whereas the divine is immaterial and free of bulk. Furthermore, these expressions in the prayer align with the experience of the people in Babylon. For, as he states in 17.137, having attained Your providence and now being stripped bare, I remove my garments, not bringing my enemies upon me in blows, bonds, or the crushing of my bones.

They say, 'Where is your God?' attributing my suffering to weakness. More ethically, when our enemies, the demons, break our bones through sin—meaning they destroy the powers of the soul—they deliberately slander God as weak toward us, hoping to strip us of hope in him so they can seize us as captives and slaves. They do this continually, every day. What must we do? We must not fall into despair, but instead hope in God’s mercy, as we will be taught in what follows.

Psalm 51, verse 7: I was brought forth in iniquity—not only in the womb, but because I accepted the deeds of iniquity, including murder and the illicit acts of a bed I violently seized. Verse 8: I have loved truth. This is the understanding: You, Lord, being true and loving truth, desire to lead us into truth through earthly means, and you cleanse us from ancient sin. You will cleanse us until we are whiter than snow; yet this cleansing for us comes through hyssop, and the energy of the Holy Spirit is likened to hyssop—it warms and removes all the filth within us.
